issue.description:
Balazs, 2026-11-13 (<issue id="9faa9b49-a208-4f6f-8b26-b2ac39709300" label="DYD-764" href="https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-764/inquisition-of-the-integrated-dytest-network" /> decision round, via the grilling agent).

## Why

Agents may not delete remote branches or worktrees, because a delete can destroy unmerged work. So Balazs is asked to run wizards to delete them, again and again, and he admits he rarely takes a second look at what's being deleted. In his words: "I don't think this should be my job … moving this to agents and making sure it is failsafe is actually probably safer than what we have today." Merged work is already safe to delete. Unmerged work is the risk.

## What it does

A dydo command that deletes a branch or worktree by first preserving it in a temporary archive, so a wrong delete loses nothing.

* **Archive first, then delete.** The branch's commits and, for a worktree, every uncommitted and untracked file go into the archive. Uncommitted files are **copied in as they are**, with no commit made. Then the branch or worktree is deleted, from GitHub too.
* **The archive lives on this machine.** Balazs's reasoning: losing work would need two failures, a wrong delete *and* a dead disk, and the dead disk is the far bigger problem anyway. A remote branch may never have been fetched here, so the command fetches it before archiving. An empty archive is a failure, not a success.
* **Kept 30 calendar days.** No background job. Archives older than 30 days are purged **only when the archive/delete command itself runs**. Nothing is deleted while nobody runs it.
* **A restore command** brings a branch or worktree back from the archive.
* Agents use this command freely. Plain `git branch -D`, `git push --delete` and worktree removal stay blocked for agents.

## Context

The three <issue id="e56c3537-1a16-4946-8ec3-99017c24bcb2" label="DYD-991" href="https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-991/daemon-stop-wait-unproven-on-windows-and-for-a-macos-non-child-zombie" /> proof branches were deleted the old way, by an owner-run wizard, on 2026-11-13. The <issue id="9faa9b49-a208-4f6f-8b26-b2ac39709300" label="DYD-764" href="https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-764/inquisition-of-the-integrated-dytest-network" /> reproduction branches (`proof/DYD-764-*`, `DYD-764-fix-*`) are cited as evidence by open tickets and wait for this command.

## Acceptance contract — proposed before crew (2026-11-16)

The original owner intent above is retained. Commission: ticket-captain / gpt-6.1-sol, high. Feature + AFK; one sequential author, no lanes. Base is pinned to `dee4861ae2691e41d9e60985e3e0ffb0c7ea987d` on `feature/dydo-4-0-0`; branch `DYD-1029-safe-delete`; PR targets `feature/dydo-4-0-0`. The local feature ref was stale at c92fbeec; the new ticket branch uses the commissioned dee4861a directly without moving the shared feature ref. Isolated host worktree: `/home/balazs/.t3/worktrees/DynaDocs/t3-8d7ada1c-88d218c54a54db07`; clean at claim. No production edits yet.

**Risk / review:** irreversible deletion after a faulty archive can destroy unique work. Require a fresh Claude spec review before production, then independent Claude + Codex whole-candidate review, at full strength. Guards stop accidents, not rogue agents. Q1–Q4 are decided below; production follows a fresh spec review. The T3 path separately owes its lifecycle research and disposable-host proof.

### Command surface

Proposed grammar:

* `dydo archive branch <name> [--remote <remote>] [--dry-run]`: archive and delete that local branch and its same-name branch on the selected remote.
* `dydo archive worktree <path> [--remote <remote>] [--dry-run]`: archive and remove one registered linked worktree, its attached local branch, and that branch on the selected remote. A detached HEAD still gets a commit archive but has no named remote branch to delete.
* `dydo archive list`: repository-local entries, ID, original target, creation/expiry, completeness and delete outcome.
* `dydo archive restore <id> [--branch <new-name>] [--path <new-path>] [--remote]`: restore locally by default without overwriting refs/directories. Explicit --remote recreates only an absent original same-name remote ref using a create-only lease.

`archive` is the delete verb: no archive-only mode or raw-delete fallback. The upstream may choose only the remote, never the ref to delete. Delete only refs/heads/<the named local branch> on that remote; a differently named upstream is reported as kept. Otherwise select origin when configured; require an explicit remote when ambiguous. Apply eligibility checks independently to the local and same-name remote refs. Explicit `--remote` selects the same-name remote branch. Local repositories with no remote work locally. Existing remote lookup/fetch failure is fatal; an absent branch is distinguished from network/auth failure. Before any remote/local destructive step for a remote-backed target, gh must establish that its same-name remote branch is neither feature/\* nor an open PR head or base. Failed, offline or incomplete lookup refuses remote deletion and keeps the local target. Unsupported remote hosts cannot silently bypass the check. Real local-bare transport tests inject the GitHub query seam. Ref names and argv are validated; no shell interpolation. Default branches, the main worktree, current/in-use/locked worktrees, and branches checked out elsewhere are refused. T3-made targets are in scope under the lifecycle contract below, superseding the blanket \~/.t3/worktrees exclusion for this command. A dry run lists intent but neither fetches, creates an archive, deletes nor purges.

### Local archive and contents

Use `<absolute git common dir>/dydo/safe-delete-archive/<UTC timestamp>-<random ID>/`, shared by all linked worktrees and separate from the existing clean archive. On this machine the root is `/home/balazs/Desktop/Projects/DynaDocs/.git/dydo/safe-delete-archive/`. No size-based eviction. Estimate archive bytes plus independent-proof scratch, including ignored files; dry-run prints both and their sum. For every affected volume, before allocations require remaining available space after archive and proof to be at least max(archive.reserveBytes, archive.reservePercent × volume total / 100). These dydo.json keys default to 5368709120 bytes (5 GiB) and 10 percent. Validate reserveBytes as nonnegative integral bytes and reservePercent as finite 0–100; invalid configuration refuses. Refusal prints both estimates, available/total space, both settings and the computed reserve. Do not credit speculative compression or purge; recheck before allocations and handle ENOSPC without deleting targets. Preflight does not lock out unrelated volume writers. Do not follow symlinks/junctions in archive ancestors or entries; refuse unsafe paths.

Each entry has versioned `manifest.json`, a self-contained `commits.bundle`, and for a worktree `files/` plus captured index/HEAD metadata. The manifest records original repository/worktree/branch/remote identities (redact URL userinfo and credential-bearing query values), every captured tip OID, timestamps, files/directories/link metadata, hashes, completion and deletion progress. Write through a unique incomplete staging entry and publish completeness only after verification.

Fetch the selected remote branch into an isolated temporary ref before archiving, even if it was never fetched here. Preserve all reachable commit history of the local tip, fetched remote tip and detached worktree HEAD, including divergent tips, with no prerequisite objects borrowed from the source repository. Include every commit named by the target branch reflog, worktree HEAD reflog and per-worktree refs (worktree, bisect and rewritten refs), retain their log/ref metadata, and list separately recoverable tips. Refuse in-progress merge, rebase, sequencer/cherry-pick, am or bisect state before any deletion. Never make a commit. Shallow history, missing objects, LFS/gitlink dependencies or unsupported filesystem objects must not be silently treated as complete: preserve their required data or refuse before any delete.

For a worktree copy its complete file state as it stands, including binary, staged/unstaged, untracked and ignored files; record tracked deletions, empty directories, executable bits and link targets. Do not traverse links outside the tree. Git administrative metadata is preserved separately rather than copied as a live repository link; preserve the index and every object it references (all conflict stages and intent-to-add metadata), including staged-only blobs absent from HEAD and the working files, so staged and unstaged states remain distinguishable. Keep these blobs in a separately verified self-contained object pack or equivalent; a copied index alone is insufficient. Initialized nested repositories/submodules or special files require complete independent preservation; otherwise refuse with an actionable reason. No build-output omission or archive size cap may cause a delete to discard a file.

### Archive-before-delete proof

A nonempty verified commit archive is mandatory even for a clean worktree or fully merged branch. No refs, empty/missing/truncated bundle, missing file, unreadable source, copy/hash mismatch, unsupported state or failed verification means nonzero exit with the original target retained. Verify the bundle and index object pack by importing into a fresh empty scratch repository and checking every recorded tip, reachable object and referenced index blob. Both commit verification and worktree/index reconstruction run without access to the source Git object store: no alternates, shared object directory or inherited Git environment. Compare reconstructed files, deletions, links, staged and unstaged status to the snapshot. Required regression: partially stage one version, change the working file again, archive/delete, run git gc --prune=now in the source, then restore and recover both versions. This proves the restore route before deletion.

Serialize archive/delete/restore/purge operations per common repository. Recheck refs and the source snapshot before destructive steps; detected changes abort. Local ref deletion is compare-and-swap against the captured OID. Remote deletion uses an explicit expected-OID lease; a remote that moved after fetching stays. For a worktree remove the remote ref first, then the verified worktree, then its local branch by compare-and-swap; never delete a branch while it is still checked out. A remote refusal leaves the local target. Every destructive step requires a published verified entry and records its result. If a later step fails, retain the archive, report exactly what remains and return nonzero; never claim atomic rollback or total success. Retry cannot overwrite newer work or discard the last recoverable copy.

Restore validates the manifest and hashes first, then reconstructs into a new path/ref. It imports the archived objects without depending on surviving source refs, recreates the working files and index, and verifies the outcome. Divergent captured tips remain separately recoverable and are listed explicitly. Existing refs/paths, corrupt data, traversal paths, linked archive containers or unsupported metadata fail without overwriting user work. Keep the archive after restore and on any failure.

### Retention and guard

Record creation and expiry explicitly; retain for 30 calendar days. Only actual `archive branch` / `archive worktree` invocations may run retention, after validating the invocation; list, restore, help and dry-run never purge. No daemon, scheduler, hook or size pressure purges entries. Purge only recognized complete entries older than the retention boundary; retain malformed/incomplete entries with diagnostics. Traverse/delete without following links; never purge outside the archive root. Tests inject a clock and cover the boundary and no-command inactivity.

The guard admits the exact dydo archive/restore/list command family for ordinary agents/subagents without owner escalation. Destructive Git subprocesses execute inside the verified command, not through a global guard bypass or environment switch. Implement and prove the explicit raw-command refusal table below; several of these rules are absent at the base, so “remain blocked” is not evidence. All direct git worktree remove forms, including plain removal, are refused under the commission's live instruction. Normal non-forced git branch -d stays compatible. Compound shell commands must still examine every segment. Existing safe merged cleanup behavior remains compatible. This ticket does not repair unrelated guard parsers.

### Windows and Linux

Same archive format and refusal contract on both. Use platform-aware path comparison; no Unix-only shell, tar or command quoting assumptions. Preserve Unix permissions and symlink targets; Windows reparse points, junctions, long paths, file locks and case collisions must either round-trip correctly or cause a pre-delete refusal. Busy-worktree checks use the established platform probes, followed by final snapshot/ref rechecks immediately before removal. These stop detected accidental concurrent use; there remains a small race after the final check, and they cannot freeze arbitrary external writers. Report this limit rather than claiming an atomic filesystem snapshot. On macOS or any platform without a supported busy probe, archive worktree refuses before deletion; branch archive remains available. A stranded Windows rename probe locks the registered worktree and reports the recovery path, following WorktreeCleaner. No platform skip counts as proof; Windows evidence must execute on Windows.

### Owned paths and exact gates

Owned: new archive command/services/models/JSON contexts, `Program.cs` registration, `Commands/HelpCommand.cs`, `Services/CompletionProvider.cs`, `Commands/GuardCommand.cs` worker allowlist, `Commands/InitCommand.cs` Codex prefix rules and their generated `.codex/rules/dydo.rules` scaffold, `Services/BashCommandAnalyzer.cs` deletion rules and refusal text, `dydo/understand/guard-system.md`, the command-reference twin `Scaffold/dydo/reference/dydo-commands.md`, narrowly required Git/guard/link/probe helpers and tests, `DynaDocs.Tests/Features/safe-delete.feature` and bindings, new `SafeDelete*Tests.cs`, test associations/platform selection data as required, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for Windows proof, command reference and verification feature-map/driver resources, and ticket evidence under `dydo/project/changelog/2026/2026-11-16/`. Existing clean behavior is a compatibility consumer, not a replacement project. Any wider ownership or acceptance change returns to the captain/admiral.

Gherkin: yes, real CLI journeys using owned local repositories and a local bare remote (no live production branch deletion). Scenarios: local/unfetched remote/divergent branch recovery; worktree full byte/index round trip without commits; detached HEAD; empty/corrupt/incomplete archive refusal; fetch/copy/read/restore failure; local/remote ref race; unsupported files and links; restore collisions; delete partial failure; 30-day retention and read-only commands; guard permits the new command and blocks raw destructive variants. Required policy scenarios: local-only default restore; explicit create-only remote restore and collision refusal; active T3 owner refusal and safe stale-thread behavior; feature/\* and PR head/base refusal, offline lookup preserving local target; both default/configured reserve branches, invalid config and dry-run archive/scratch byte estimates. Assert init-generated Codex prefix rules admit the actual archive forms without owner escalation. Add eligibility Scenario Outline rows for local default, remote default, unknown remote default, main/current/locked/in-use worktree, branch checked out elsewhere, missing/prunable target, and live T3 owner; each refusal proves local refs, remote refs and files intact. Resolve the selected remote's live default with git ls-remote --symref <remote> HEAD; do not copy MergedBranchJudge's stale-cache fallback for destructive decisions. Unknown remote default refuses remote deletion.

Before expensive runs: prove branch/base/clean state, tool/runtime pins and nonzero intended discovery. Record exact SHA or dirty-byte identity, argv, environment, exit and raw result path for every run. Use the existing shared gate lock outside a memory cap; Codex concurrency around 8, fewer on 429. Each probe: systemd scope MemoryMax=4G, MemorySwapMax=0, OOMPolicy=continue, timeout 120. Each gate: 8G, timeout 3600. Use the nearest user-manager agent slice from /proc/self/cgroup. .NET env: MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1 DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER=0 UseSharedCompilation=false. Never raise a cap after a hit.

* Building: focused `dotnet test DynaDocs.Tests/DynaDocs.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~SafeDelete --logger trx`, plus selected reached clean/Git/guard suites identified before code; include executable Gherkin scenarios in discovery.
* Each committed hop: all own/reached Light plus `.static-gates/python/bin/python DynaDocs.Tests/coverage/gap_check.py gate static --stack dotnet`; widen stacks if executable changes reach them.
* Final candidate: `.static-gates/python/bin/python DynaDocs.Tests/coverage/gap_check.py gate coverage --stack dotnet` (the facade lacks ticket selection, so whole-stack coverage remains owed), and `.static-gates/python/bin/python DynaDocs.Tests/coverage/gap_check.py gate mutation --since dee4861ae2691e41d9e60985e3e0ffb0c7ea987d --stack dotnet`. An unavailable mutation capability is a named gap, never success. Determine applicable Heavy from actual reach; dormant guard performance proofs run only if their declared trigger applies.
* Native Linux and Windows round trips, failure/ref-race proofs, and Windows guard/lock/link checks; host CI on the actual candidate/merge ref. Existing verify-dydo driver is Windows-only and has no archive journey yet: extend its map/driver where needed rather than claiming an unsupported Linux drive.
* Captain reruns the writer's actual proof recipe; independent first-round Claude + Codex review. No production change authored by the captain. Offer only with required gates and review accounted for.

### Recorded rulings (2026-11-16)

* Q1, admiral: restore locally by default; explicit --remote creates only an absent original same-name remote ref with a create-only lease.
* Q2, Balazs verbatim: "If they're most worktrees I'm asked to delete then yes. But we should make sure that we don't break T3 or mess with it in any meaningful way." T3 targets ARE in scope under the lifecycle contract below.
* Q3, admiral: refuse remote feature/\* and open-PR head/base deletion. Failed/offline PR lookup refuses and retains the local target. gh dependency accepted.
* Q4, admiral: keep every file, ignored included. Dry-run prints archive and independent-proof scratch estimates. Default configurable reserve: max(5 GiB, 10% of volume); print the numbers in refusals. <issue id="74cc2ed5-a670-438d-b02c-64ad16736d41" label="DYD-1107" href="https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-1107/safe-delete-spec-define-a-free-space-reserve-before-archiving" /> is closed as a contract choice; runtime proof is owed here.
* Q5, admiral: [DYD-1113](<https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-1113>) is the Backlog adoption follow-up, blocked by <issue id="4ffab092-4f99-4b5c-8ddb-3e66d1419a52" label="DYD-1029" href="https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-1029/a-safe-delete-dydo-command-archive-a-branch-or-worktree-for-30-days" />.

### T3 lifecycle and native proof

Before touching a T3-made target, establish how the running T3 version tracks it and handles folder disappearance from its own source and supported APIs. Enumerate all threads with that canonical worktreePath, including delegated/shared-worktree children and relevant archived records, then read settled state and activeRunId. Refuse any target used by a live non-settled active-run thread, live provider session or open terminal; refuse where authoritative ownership/activity is unavailable. Recheck just before removal. Never remove this captain's or another active thread's tree.

Prefer a T3-supported release/removal route; t3_worktree_handoff creates a worktree for the current thread and is not a release API. Do not modify T3's database, invent APIs, clear historical thread records or mark another thread settled. Before enabling deletion, prove the actual path in a disposable T3-created worktree (a captain-dispatched proof child with isolation:worktree; no new top-level thread). Record target/thread/branch identity and initial list/read health; refusal while active; successful archive and source-independent restore proof; inactive deletion; subsequent thread list/read health, no server crash and sane stale-thread metadata. Do not count T3's automatic recreation as archive restoration. Keep every other worktree intact.

If no supported/verifiable route can delete without breaking T3, return the named finding and leave that target intact; the rest of the command may ship, as explicitly commissioned. This is a proof gate, not permission to ignore T3 research.

Discovery on Nightfury, T3 0.1.9: thread records retain worktreePath after removal; thread/ref/title reads fall back to the project root when the path is absent. ProviderTurnStartService recreates a missing managed worktree on a later run from the surviving branch, remote-tracking branch or project base; that does not restore archived content. Report this distinction; restore refuses a replacement path/ref collision. StorageCleanup already removes inactive managed worktrees while retaining thread history and checking thread/session/terminal activity. The bundled VCS remove endpoint exists, but the exposed worktree MCP tools are list/status/handoff; no public release API is established. The public t3 thread list CLI omits subagents, so it is not sufficient ownership proof on its own.

Preserve excerpts/digests in durable ticket evidence before relying on /tmp longevity.

### Spec-review corrections and raw-command Scenario Outline

Required remote-target regression: a local branch tracking origin/feature/dydo-4-0-0 while its own name differs archives only its own local/same-name remote tips, reports the differently named upstream as kept, and leaves the integration remote ref unchanged. No similarly named branch inference is allowed.

Prerequisite probe (Linux captain session): .NET SDK 10.0.303 and [Microsoft.NETCore.App](<http://Microsoft.NETCore.App>) 10.0.14 are present; python3.14 exists. The local assurance venv remains unprovisioned and must be set up before gates; these version checks are not runtime proof. Agent slice observed: app-t3code-agents-cbc6c2286251.slice.

The first review is FAIL (three blockers); its full block is retained in the ticket discussion. This amendment corrects the spec, not an implementation: all runtime gates remain owed. The existing clean command is a compatibility consumer; its internal Git subprocesses are not raw agent calls.

Scenario Outline: raw destructive Git stays outside the safe archive route.
Given an ordinary agent or subagent invokes the command through each supported shell hook, when the guard reads <command>, then it refuses before Git runs and points to dydo archive. Include git global options (-C, -c, --git-dir), absolute Git executable paths, supported option permutations and compound-shell segments in the cases the existing parser supports. New coverage/rules are explicitly owed for force-branch deletion, update-ref deletion, global-option remote deletion, deletion refspecs and plain worktree removal; existing direct push-delete and forced-remove coverage must remain green.

| command | verdict |
| -- | -- |
| git branch -D topic | refuse |
| git branch -d -f topic | refuse |
| git branch --delete --force topic | refuse |
| git update-ref -d refs/heads/topic | refuse |
| git push origin --delete topic | refuse |
| git -C repo push origin --delete topic | refuse |
| git push origin :refs/heads/topic | refuse |
| git push origin +:refs/heads/topic | refuse |
| git push --prune origin | refuse |
| git push --mirror origin | refuse |
| git worktree remove tree | refuse |
| git worktree remove --force tree | refuse |
| git branch -d merged-topic | allow absent another rule |
| dydo archive branch topic | allow absent another rule |
| dydo archive worktree tree | allow absent another rule |
| dydo archive list | allow absent another rule |
| dydo archive restore ID | allow absent another rule |
| dydo archive list && git branch -D topic | refuse |

Nits 9 and 10 are accepted into the contract: redact remote credentials; delete remote, worktree, then local branch. No deferred nit remains in this spec.

### Fresh spec-review clarifications (PASS follow-up, 2026-11-16)

These close the fresh spec review's four should findings and two nits; the accepted outcome and safety gates are unchanged.

1. T3 recognition uses the default server worktreesDir, configured worktreesDirectory, every previousWorktreesDirectories root and any normalized path containing /.t3/worktrees/. Expand home paths, require valid host-absolute non-root directories and compare canonical paths with platform-appropriate casing; conservative containment may classify extra paths as managed rather than miss a managed target. T3 0.1.9's canonical management helper requires exactly two path segments under each resolved root; its history-recognition helper also accepts the substring form. Include both in the defensive recognition seam. If T3 settings exist but cannot be read/validated authoritatively, refuse worktree deletion rather than assume an ordinary target. Add the custom non-default/previous-root T3 eligibility rows.
2. Gherkin uses an injected T3 ownership/activity interface: active owner → refusal with refs/files intact; ownership unavailable → refusal; settled/inactive target → eligible only if the T3 route has been enabled after native proof and all other checks pass. Gherkin must not fake or claim stale-thread health, list/read behavior or absence of host crashes; only the disposable T3-host proof establishes those outcomes.
3. Restore mapping is deterministic. For a branch archive, the primary restored branch uses the original local tip, or the captured same-name remote tip when no local tip existed. For a worktree archive its saved HEAD is primary; preserve detached HEAD unless --branch explicitly requests attachment. --branch renames only the primary branch. Every captured tip also has a stable archive tip ID and bundle ref; restoration recreates all of them under refs/dydo-restored/<archive-id>/<tip-id>, using create-only ref operations. list and restore print the IDs/OIDs/ref mapping. Conflicting pre-existing recovery refs refuse unless they already point to the identical archived OID. The divergent-history scenario must recover both the remote tip and a reflog-only tip through restore and prove both remain reachable after source garbage collection; imported unreferenced objects are insufficient. The original same-name remote tip is the sole source for explicit --remote republishing, even when the local and remote tips diverged.
4. Owned paths additionally include Models/DydoConfig.cs, dydo/reference/configuration.md (active schema example and Fields table), and source-generated JSON configuration registration reached by the new archive settings. The nearest existing dydo.json is read; this ticket does not rewrite user config to inject defaults. Verification driver edits are Python changes and owe applicable Python static/coverage gates in addition to dotnet.

Nit 5 accepted: in a repository with no remote, protect the main worktree's symbolic HEAD branch and any explicitly configured init.defaultBranch name. If neither provides an authoritative local default, refuse branch deletion; never invent a main/master fallback. A target's own main-worktree occupancy is independently refused.

Nit 6 accepted: dry-run never fetches. It labels the remote-object component unknown/lower-bound when the remote tip is not present locally, and does not present that as a complete total. A real run checks the configured free-space reserve before fetch and rechecks immediately after the controlled fetch, then computes the complete archive-plus-proof allocation bound before archive writes. Fetch failure, quota/disk failure or a post-fetch reserve shortfall never permits deletion. Document that remote transfer size is not promised before transfer.

### DECIDED — mutation availability and review grading (admiral, 2026-11-17)

The changed-code mutation command remains required to run and be recorded accurately. Its current exit 2 (`UNAVAILABLE: Pending DYD-103`) is an inherited, fail-closed capability gap owned by <issue id="6c8c77ec-e009-41bb-a198-4a9b0c00c01c" label="DYD-103" href="https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-103/implement-isolated-mutation-assurance-for-c-python-and-javascript" />, never a passing gate. By the admiral's Project-wide ruling this unavailable result does not hold the <issue id="4ffab092-4f99-4b5c-8ddb-3e66d1419a52" label="DYD-1029" href="https://linear.app/bodnar-balazs/issue/DYD-1029/a-safe-delete-dydo-command-archive-a-branch-or-worktree-for-30-days" /> offer. Retain meaningful RED proofs and fresh cross-vendor review. This explicitly reconciles the earlier final-gate obligation and Codex review finding 4; it does not waive or report mutation success.

For round 2 and later, apply DR 058: a blocker means the intended case is wrong; a test-only gap with correct behavior is a should. The fork-branch PR-head and missing restored configuration findings are actual behavior defects and remain blockers until fixed. Required native Windows execution remains owed.
